english.title: Attempt arson
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to commit arson in that without lawful excuse you attempted to

(A)_[destroy]_
(B)_[damage]_

by fire **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..) belonging to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempted to commit arson in that without lawful excuse
by attempting to destroy / damage
by fire property with intent
to destroy / damage it or
being reckless as to whether
such property was destroyed / damaged

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Property attempted to be damaged/destroyed must NOT belong to the defendant(s).
(ii) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where the attempted damage is to a spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) See the substantive offence at H470

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
